capabilities.target: quicknotes hosted sync service operated by the tool's third-party author
any Slack channel reachable by the bot token, including channels shared with external organizations

inputs.source: User request typed into the desktop client
Tool names and descriptions returned by quicknotes_mcp's tools/list response

elements.name: Human user of the desktop client

controls.name: First-call approval, remembered as 'always allow'
controls.decay_rationale: This approval fires once per tool and is then remembered; subsequent calls to the same tool proceed without any review. It is not wired as an ongoing approval gate on any capability and earns no residual credit (control_decay.md: a remembered approval is not a gate).

controls.name: Filesystem MCP server scoped to C:/Users/dev
controls.decay_rationale: Limits the filesystem server to the user's home directory rather than the whole disk, but ~/.aws/credentials lies inside that same directory, so the scope does not exclude the sensitive sink this finding depends on.

controls.name: Tool definition pinning/hashing for third-party MCP servers
controls.decay_rationale: Not present; quicknotes_mcp is installed via npx -y quicknotes-mcp@latest with no pinning, hashing, or review of tool definition changes.

controls.name: Injection scanning of third-party tool descriptions and outputs
controls.decay_rationale: Not present. Even if added, a classifier-based scanner is partially dependent since adaptively worded injected instructions can evade pattern or semantic detection.

controls.name: Filesystem server excludes credential directories
controls.decay_rationale: Not present. Would need to exclude ~/.aws, ~/.ssh, and similar paths from the filesystem server's allowed root to sever the credential-read step of the tool-poisoning path.

controls.name: Network egress allowlist for third-party MCP servers
controls.decay_rationale: Not present; quicknotes_mcp's hosted sync destination is not restricted to any allowlist.

controls.name: Slack channel allowlist excluding externally shared channels
controls.decay_rationale: Not present; the Slack bot token can post to any channel the bot is a member of, including channels shared with external organizations.

controls.name: Treat quicknotes output as untrusted; block direct chaining into Slack posts without review
controls.decay_rationale: Not present. Even if implemented via a classifier or heuristic gate, a sufficiently novel injected instruction in tool output could still evade detection, so this would only narrow, not sever, the path.

controls.name: Tamper-evident action audit log
controls.decay_rationale: Not present; no artifact describes logging or provenance for any tool call.

controls.name: Unattended step and runtime cap
controls.decay_rationale: Not present; max_unattended_steps and max_runtime_minutes are both unset.

findings.title: MCP tool poisoning (TC1 lethal trifecta) exfiltrates AWS credentials via quicknotes_mcp.add_note

attack_path.note: quicknotes_mcp's add_note tool description contains an <IMPORTANT> block instructing the model to read ~/.aws/credentials and pass its contents in the "context" argument, and to not mention this step to the user
agent reads the AWS credentials file as instructed by the poisoned tool description
agent calls add_note with credential contents in the context argument, which is transmitted to the third-party author-operated hosted sync service

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: quicknotes_mcp's tools/list response changes on any @latest update (no diff or pin to detect it), or desk-assistant's model is upgraded and begins complying more readily with embedded instructions.

evidence.observation: add_note tool description contains an <IMPORTANT> block instructing the model to read ~/.aws/credentials and pass its contents in the context argument before calling add_note, and to not mention this step to the user
quicknotes_mcp is launched with npx -y quicknotes-mcp@latest, no version pin
quicknotes_mcp is a community package published by an individual and calls a hosted sync service run by its author

recommendations.action: Pin and hash quicknotes_mcp's tool definitions; block and alert on any change instead of silently accepting @latest updates.

Scan third-party MCP tool descriptions for embedded imperative instructions before exposing them to the model, and strip or quarantine any that attempt to direct tool use or suppress disclosure to the user.
Scope the filesystem MCP server away from credential directories (~/.aws, ~/.ssh, environment files) rather than granting read access to the entire user profile.
Restrict quicknotes_mcp to an egress allowlist so arguments cannot reach destinations outside an approved set.

findings.title: Untrusted quicknotes_mcp output can redirect the agent to post sensitive data via slack.post_message to externally shared channels

attack_path.note: quicknotes_mcp is run via @latest with no pinning and is operated by an individual third party; its output is equally capable of carrying embedded instructions as its tool description already demonstrated
agent posts via the Slack bot, which can reach any channel including those shared with external organizations, with a broadly scoped bot token

forecast.watch_signal: Slack bot token scope widened, new externally-shared channels added, or desk-assistant's model upgraded and begins following tool-output-embedded instructions more readily.

evidence.observation: the same server that embeds hostile instructions in a tool description is also the source of in.notes_output, with no description-vs-output distinction enforced by the client
The Slack bot can post to any channel, including channels shared with external organizations
slack-mcp is installed via npx -y slack-mcp@latest with a bot token in SLACK_BOT_TOKEN, and no channel scoping is declared

recommendations.action: Restrict the Slack bot token's channel scope to an allowlist that excludes channels shared with external organizations.
Treat all quicknotes_mcp tool output as untrusted data; do not let it directly drive further tool calls (such as slack.post_message) without a human-reviewed step bound to the original request.
Log every outbound Slack post with its destination channel and the upstream data source that produced its content, so cross-tool-driven posts are distinguishable from user-directed ones.

findings.title: No attributable record of agent actions across file reads, note syncs, or Slack posts

forecast.watch_signal: Any increase in autonomy or unattended steps without a corresponding introduction of action logging.

evidence.observation: No logging, audit trail, or action-provenance mechanism is described for any of the three MCP servers or for the desktop client itself

recommendations.action: Add a tamper-evident log of every tool call (reads, note syncs, Slack posts) including arguments, timestamp, and the triggering source (user request vs. third-party tool output), retained independent of the agent process.

findings.title: No step, runtime, or spend limit bounds unattended agent execution

forecast.watch_signal: Observed task runtimes or step counts per session trending upward without a corresponding cap being added.

evidence.locator: autonomy design (absence of fields in runtime notes)
evidence.observation: No max_unattended_steps, max_runtime_minutes, or spend cap is described anywhere in the artifacts; after the first 'always allow,' every subsequent tool call proceeds without review or bound

recommendations.action: Set an explicit maximum number of unattended tool calls and a runtime ceiling per task, enforced by the client or orchestrator rather than the model.

stride_coverage.rationale: desk-assistant is the local subject agent itself; this design describes no mechanism by which another party impersonates the agent process to its own user or connected servers.
Local npx-spawned subprocess communicating over stdio; no remote network identity to spoof within this design.
mcp.json pins no version for @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem (installed via npx -y, i.e. always latest); artifacts do not describe any package integrity verification for this server.
No information on filesystem server resource limits or failure handling is provided in the artifacts.

The server grants read access to a fixed local directory; the privilege escalation risk is carried by what is read and sent elsewhere, captured under finding.tool_poisoning's elevation_of_privilege entry on el.desk_assistant.
Artifacts do not describe how slack-mcp authenticates to the Slack API beyond the presence of a SLACK_BOT_TOKEN env var; no peer identity verification detail is given.
slack-mcp is also installed via npx -y with no version pin (slack-mcp@latest); no tools/list content was provided to assess whether its definitions contain embedded instructions.
No rate limit information for Slack posting is provided in the artifacts.
No information on whether the author-operated hosted sync service logs or attributes the requests it receives.
The user authenticates to the local desktop client; this design provides no channel through which a remote party impersonates the user to desk-assistant.
User-side action attribution is outside this design's scope; the relevant audit gap is on the agent side, captured in finding.no_audit_trail.
This inbound flow carries tool metadata into the agent; it does not itself carry user or credential data outward. Outward disclosure is captured on el.flow_notes_add and el.flow_slack_post.
No information on volume, retries, or error handling for tools/list retrieval.
This inbound flow carries data into the agent; outward disclosure is captured on el.flow_slack_post.
No information on volume or error handling for quicknotes output.
Artifacts do not describe transport security (e.g. TLS) for requests to the quicknotes hosted sync service.
No rate or size limit described for add_note calls.
Artifacts do not describe transport security details beyond standard Slack API usage.
No rate limit information for Slack posting is provided.
This design only models a read path to the credentials file; no write or modify path to it is described.
A local single-user credentials file is not a shared resource subject to agent-induced denial of service in this design.

rating.rationale: Two present findings reach critical: a confirmed MCP tool-poisoning attack (quicknotes_mcp's add_note description instructs the model to read and exfiltrate ~/.aws/credentials) and a closely related risk that quicknotes_mcp's own output can similarly redirect the agent to post sensitive data to Slack channels shared with external organizations. Neither path is mitigated by the only declared control (a once-per-tool approval that is remembered as 'always allow' and therefore earns no residual credit per control_decay.md), and the filesystem server's directory scope does not exclude credential files. Two further property findings (no attributable action log; no step or runtime cap) independently reach high. Although the desktop client's first-call approval resembles A2 (approval on sensitive actions), approvals are remembered per tool and are not reviewed on subsequent calls, so autonomy is scored as A3_act_then_report per rubric section 3. No forecast trigger changes any finding's tier, since essentially no structural controls currently constrain these paths; the recommended fixes (pin tool definitions, scan descriptions and output for embedded instructions, exclude credential directories from filesystem access, restrict Slack channel scope, add an audit log and a step/runtime cap) are what would bring residual down.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration captured in mcp.json, the quicknotes_mcp tools/list response, and the provided runtime notes; it does not reflect observed runtime behavior of the agent or any of the three MCP servers.

No agent system prompt was provided, so instruction-level issues (ambiguous goals, conflicting directives, unbounded scope) could not be assessed; only tool-level and protocol-level risks are covered.

No tools/list content was provided for the filesystem or slack-mcp servers, so tool poisoning risk from those two servers could not be directly confirmed and is recorded as not_assessed rather than as a finding.
quicknotes_mcp's hosted sync service behavior (what it actually does with received data) was not independently verified; risk is inferred from its documented instruction to exfiltrate credentials.
